title: Construction of 28.3 MW Middle Chameliya Hydropower Project Set to Begin in Darchula
content:
Sudurpashchim Province is expanding its renewable energy capacity as preparations begin for the construction of a new 28.30 megawatt hydropower plant on the Chameliya River. Promoted by Darchula Power Company, the Middle Chameliya Hydropower Project will be located in Marma Rural Municipality of Darchula district, situated within the protected Api Nampa Conservation Area.

The project has reached several key regulatory and financial milestones to pave the way for development.The Department of Electricity Development granted the generation license for the run-of-river project in March 2025. Following an initial Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) approval in March 2024, developer Chameliya Power Limited secured permission to conduct a Supplementary EIA to assess minor layout revisions and structural relocations on the river's left bank.The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Environment recently issued a public notice requesting feedback on the supplementary study.

Commercial preparations for the plant are already in place.The developer signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) in October 2023 and completed financial closure in June 2025. All electricity generated by the project will be fed directly into the national grid via the NEA's nearby Balach Substation.

Located approximately 30 kilometers northwest of Gokuleshwar, the plant will operate between two existing projects on the same river, athe 40 MW Upper Chameliya project upstream and the 30 MW Chameliya Khola project downstream.Once operational, the Middle Chameliya plant is projected to supply 118.52 gigawatt hours (GWh) of electricity during the wet season and 67.10 GWh during the dry season.

With an estimated total investment of NPR 6.23 billion (approx. Rs 6.236 billion), construction is targeted for completion within three years.

title: NEPSE Opens Applications for Chief Executive Officer; Finance Ministry Invites Qualified Candidates
content:
The Government of Nepal has formally initiated the recruitment process for the vacant post of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE), inviting applications from qualified Nepali citizens through an open competitive selection process.

A public notice published by the Selection and Recommendation Committee formed to appoint the CEO states that interested candidates must submit their applications within 15 days from the date of publication. Applications, along with a sealed business action plan, must be submitted during office hours to the Financial Sector Management and Corporation Coordination Division under the Ministry of Finance at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu.

The recruitment process follows the recently approved Procedure for the Selection and Recommendation of the Chief Executive Officer of Nepal Stock Exchange Limited, 2083.

According to the vacancy notice, candidates must possess at least a Master's degree from a recognised institution in Economics, Commerce, Finance, Management, Information Technology, Business, or Law, or hold a Chartered Accountancy (CA) qualification or an equivalent degree.

Applicants are also required to have a minimum of 15 years of professional experience in the capital market, financial sector, or management, including at least seven years in a managerial position.

The notice clarifies that a managerial position refers to at least a Second Class Officer level in the Government of Nepal or an equivalent role, or executive leadership positions up to two levels below the chief executive in a company or organised institution.

Applicants must be Nepali citizens aged between 30 and 65 years as of the application deadline.

In addition, candidates must not be disqualified under the CEO Selection Procedure, 2083, or the Standards for Appointment and Nomination of Office Bearers and Members of Public Bodies under the Ministry of Finance, 2073 (as amended).

The notice states that the following individuals are ineligible:1. Non-Nepali citizens.2. Persons convicted of corruption, money laundering, human trafficking, narcotics offences, crimes involving archaeological artefacts or protected wildlife, or other criminal offences involving moral turpitude.3. Individuals blacklisted under prevailing laws who have not completed three years since being removed from the blacklist.4. Persons holding permanent residency in a foreign country.5. Individuals currently engaged in contractual work with a public institution in the capacity of an executive head.6. Persons declared mentally unfit.

Besides the standard application documents, applicants are required to submit a detailed business action plan outlining their vision and strategy for leading Nepal's only stock exchange.

The business action plan must be submitted in three sealed copies. The outer envelope must clearly mention the applicant's name and indicate that it contains the application and business action plan for the post of NEPSE CEO.

Applicants must also submit all documents specified under the CEO Selection Procedure, including self-certified copies of academic and professional certificates, prescribed application forms, and two passport-sized photographs.

Candidates must deposit a non-refundable application fee of Rs. 5,000 at the designated revenue account of the Ministry of Finance through the Singha Durbar branch of Rastriya Banijya Bank and submit the original payment voucher along with the application.

The selected CEO will receive salary, allowances, and other benefits as determined by the Government of Nepal.

The Selection and Recommendation Committee will assess applicants based on their academic qualifications, professional experience, business action plan, and presentation before recommending suitable candidates for appointment.

The committee has reserved the right to reject any application with or without assigning reasons. It has also warned that any applicant found submitting false information or forged documents will have their application cancelled and may face legal action under prevailing laws.

The vacancy marks the formal commencement of the process to appoint a new chief executive for NEPSE, a key institution in Nepal's capital market that has been operating without a permanent CEO.

title: Finance Minister Wagle Directs SEBON to Strengthen Regulatory Quality and Accelerate Capital Market Development
content:
Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle visited the office of the Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) on Monday and guided the development and expansion of the country’s capital market.

The programme held on the occasion of the minister’s visit was attended by Finance Secretary Dr Ghanshyam Upadhyaya, senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, members of the SEBON Board of Directors and senior officials of the securities regulator.

SEBON Chairman Dr Gopal Prasad Bhatta welcomed Finance Minister Wagle and other distinguished guests on behalf of the Board. During the programme, Chairman Bhatta briefed the minister on the initiatives undertaken by SEBON to promote the development and expansion of Nepal’s capital market.

Chairman Bhatta informed the minister that SEBON has prepared and begun implementing a Capital Market Development Blueprint as its overall vision for the development of the capital market. He also stated that the Board has initiated the implementation of the capital market policy and action plan for the fiscal year 2083/84.

According to Bhatta, SEBON is preparing consultative papers, rules and directives related to various primary and secondary market instruments and activities outlined in the current fiscal year’s policy and programme. These include initial public offerings (IPOs), intraday trading, margin lending and short selling, among other areas.

The Board plans to prepare the necessary consultative papers, rules and directives by the month of Shrawan 2083. Following the collection of suggestions and feedback, consultations with stakeholders are expected to begin from Bhadra 2083. The policies, rules and directives will then be reviewed and amended as necessary based on stakeholder feedback.

During the programme, the SEBON chairman also briefed the finance minister on the existing challenges and problems facing Nepal’s capital market. He requested the Ministry of Finance to facilitate the Board in addressing those challenges and provide necessary support for effective policy formulation and implementation.

Bhatta also stressed the need to effectively implement policy programmes to enhance the motivation of SEBON employees and strengthen the institutional capacity of the regulator.

Addressing the programme, Finance Minister Wagle directed SEBON to advance capital market development by improving regulatory quality and maintaining high ethical standards.

He said the appointment of new leadership at SEBON and the Board’s decision to move forward with a long-term strategy had sent a positive message to the market. According to him, efforts to accelerate capital market development have also generated positive expectations among investors.

Minister Wagle stressed that SEBON should develop into a strong regulator with a stature comparable to the role played by Nepal Rastra Bank in the country’s financial system.

He also urged the Board to develop itself as a robust and credible regulator without deviating from its core responsibilities. With the rapid growth of dematerialised (demat) accounts in Nepal, investor expectations have increased significantly, and the minister called for institutional development and regulatory capacity-building to match those expectations.

The finance minister further emphasised the importance of adopting a political-economy perspective while formulating capital market policies. He said that policies should be developed after adequate consultation and discussion with all concerned stakeholders to ensure the sustainable development of the capital market.

Minister Wagle said the changes in SEBON’s working approach under the new government and new leadership had conveyed a positive message to investors. He assured that the Government of Nepal would provide all necessary facilitation and support for regulatory and legal reforms aimed at strengthening the capital market.

The minister’s visit and directives come at a time when SEBON has announced plans to introduce and reform several capital market instruments and regulatory frameworks, intending to strengthen market infrastructure, expand investment opportunities, and improve the overall efficiency and credibility of Nepal’s capital market.

title: Supreme Court Orders Separate Reserve Fund for Premium Share Proceeds in Himalayan Reinsurance Case
content:
The Supreme Court has directed that amounts collected above the face value of shares issued at a premium be kept separately in a dedicated reserve fund, citing the need to ensure compliance with the law and protect investors’ interests.

The directive was issued while deciding a writ petition related to the initial public offering (IPO) of Himalayan Reinsurance Limited (HRL), which had issued shares to the general public at a premium price.

A joint bench of Justices Dr Manoj Kumar Sharma and Shree Kanta Paudel ruled that the responsibility of regulatory authorities does not end with merely granting permission to issue shares at a premium.

The Supreme Court stated that regulatory bodies must thoroughly examine the prospectus and other documents submitted by an issuing company before approving a premium-priced share issue.

In the case of Himalayan Reinsurance, the court noted that regulators were required to ensure that the interests of investors were protected and that all legal requirements were properly fulfilled before approving.

The ruling has emphasised that the Nepal Insurance Authority and the Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) must exercise greater diligence when approving premium-priced share issues in the future.

The court has also directed the authorities not to allow the issuance of shares at premium prices in violation of existing laws.

The Supreme Court has issued a directive to the Nepal Insurance Authority, SEBON and Himalayan Reinsurance to coordinate and establish an appropriate mechanism for keeping the amount collected above the face value of shares in a separate reserve fund.

Under the court’s interpretation, the amount collected above the face value of shares should not be treated as ordinary income that can be freely distributed or spent by the company.

In simple terms, Himalayan Reinsurance issued shares with a face value of NPR 100 at NPR 206 per share, including a premium of NPR 106. The court’s directive means that the additional amount collected above the face value must be managed separately in accordance with the applicable legal provisions.

The court has directed the concerned regulators to coordinate and make necessary arrangements for the management of such premium proceeds.

The provisions of the Companies Act, 2063, and the Insurance Act, 2079, have been considered in relation to the management and use of premium proceeds. The ruling indicates that a clear regulatory framework is required to determine how such funds should be held and under what circumstances they may be utilised.

Although the Supreme Court issued important directives to the regulators, it did not invalidate Himalayan Reinsurance’s IPO.

The court dismissed the writ petition filed against the company’s premium-priced share issue, concluding that there was no sufficient basis to cancel the share issuance and allotment process.

The court also considered the fact that the IPO and share allotment had already been completed while the writ petition was under consideration. Therefore, it found no justification for cancelling the completed issuance and allotment process.

The ruling noted that Himalayan Reinsurance had fulfilled the required criteria for issuing shares at a premium.

According to the judgment, the company had remained profitable for the previous three consecutive financial years, its net worth per share was higher than its paid-up capital, and it had fulfilled relevant requirements, including credit-rating criteria.

The court also interpreted the provisions of the Insurance Act, 2079, alongside the Companies Act, 2063, and the Securities Registration and Issue Regulations, 2073.

While the Insurance Act requires companies to call for 100 percent of the face value when inviting the public to purchase shares, company and securities laws allow eligible institutions to issue shares at a price higher than their face value, subject to the fulfilment of prescribed conditions.

The Companies Act defines shares sold above their face value as premium shares, while the Securities Registration and Issue Regulations specify the conditions that an institution must fulfil to issue shares at a premium.

The Supreme Court’s ruling has broader implications for premium-priced share issues in Nepal’s capital market.

Although the court did not cancel Himalayan Reinsurance’s IPO, it has clearly highlighted the responsibility of regulatory authorities to conduct detailed scrutiny of a company’s financial condition, prospectus, legal basis and other relevant documents before approving.

The ruling has also stressed that regulatory approval should not weaken corporate governance or undermine investor confidence in the securities market.

The court has effectively directed the Nepal Insurance Authority and SEBON to ensure greater transparency and stronger regulatory oversight in future premium share issues.

The decision is expected to influence how premium proceeds are managed by companies and how regulators coordinate to protect investors and ensure that funds collected above the face value of shares are used in accordance with the law.

title: Nepal Rastra Bank Penalizes Three Financial Institutions Over Regulatory Breaches
content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the country’s central bank, has taken disciplinary action against three financial institutions, Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, and Reliance Finance for breaking regulatory rules during the fourth quarter of the fiscal year 2082/83.

Narayani Development Bankran into trouble over its lending practices. When NRB previously removed the bank from its list of troubled institutions, it set a strict condition: total loans and credit facilities to any single customer, business, or connected group of clients could not exceed 10% of the bank's core capital. An investigation revealed that the bank violated this threshold during the 2024/25 fiscal year (FY 2081/82). As a result, the central bank issued an official caution to Bishnu Regmi, who served as Chief Executive Officer during that period, instructing him to ensure such errors do not happen again.

Saptakoshi Development Bankwas called out for severe internal management failures following a routine inspection based on its financial statements from mid-October 2025 (Ashwin 2082). Inspectors discovered missing cash in the bank’s vault along with unauthorized employee access to customer accounts. The central bank noted that even after learning about these breaches, Saptakoshi's management failed to conduct a thorough investigation, punish those responsible, or update its internal control policies to prevent future abuse. The institution was issued a formal warning to fix its operational oversight.

Reliance Financefaced a financial penalty for failing to maintain its required cash reserve levels between February 22, 2026, and April 18, 2026 (Phagun 10, 2082 to Baishakh 5, 2083). Because the company fell short of keeping the mandated amount of liquid cash on hand, the central bank fined it NPR 2,924.48 in accordance with current financial regulations.

title: Himalayan Bullion’s Revenue Soars to Rs. 9.79 Billion in First Nine Months of FY2026
content:
Himalayan Bullion Company Limited (HBCL), Nepal’s only organised participant in the silver bullion trading market, has reported a sharp improvement in its business performance during the first nine months of the fiscal year 2026, with revenue soaring to Rs. 9.79 billion, driven by rising global silver prices and strong demand for investment-grade silver.

The company's operational scale expanded significantly during the first nine months of FY2026 (unaudited period ended mid-April 2026), leading to a marked improvement in its financial risk profile, supported by a stronger capital structure and enhanced debt servicing indicators.

According to a recent report by CARE Ratings Nepal Limited, the company generated Rs. 9.789 billion in operating income during the first nine months of FY2026, a substantial increase from Rs. 302 million recorded in the entire FY2025. The rating agency, however, noted that the sustainability of this strong operational performance remains to be seen.

Despite the decline in FY2025, HBCL reported a remarkable turnaround during the first nine months of FY2026, with operating income soaring to Rs. 9.79 billion. The sharp growth was primarily driven by a significant rise in global silver prices and higher demand for investment-grade silver, along with increased trading volumes.

The company's operating profitability showed gradual improvement over the review period. The Profit Before Interest, Lease Rentals, Depreciation and Tax (PBILDT) margin increased to 4.23% in FY2025 from 3.77% in FY2024. During the first nine months of FY2026, the margin further improved to 5.64%, supported by bulk silver imports that reduced logistics costs and premium charges. The improvement in profitability significantly boosted the company's Gross Cash Accruals (GCA), which increased to Rs. 505 million during the first nine months of FY2026 from Rs. 42 million in FY2025.

HBCL's capital structure improved considerably during the review period. The company's Overall Gearing Ratio, which measures debt relative to shareholders' equity, declined from 1.22 times in FY2024 to 1.01 times in FY2025. Following fresh capital infusion by promoters, the ratio further improved to 0.48 times during the first nine months of FY2026. The company's equity base nearly doubled to Rs. 307 million by mid-April 2026, strengthening its financial position.

HBCL's debt servicing indicators also witnessed notable improvement. The Interest Coverage Ratio remained modest at 1.10 times in FY2025 compared to 1.20 times in FY2024. However, the ratio surged to 54.73 times during the first nine months of FY2026, reflecting the substantial increase in operating earnings.

Similarly, the Total Debt to Gross Cash Accruals Ratio improved significantly from 45.88 times in FY2024 to 2.84 times in FY2025 and further to 0.55 times during the first nine months of FY2026. CARE Ratings Nepal noted that while the company has achieved a significant scale-up in operations and profitability, the sustainability of this performance remains to be seen.

Established in 2000, Himalayan Bullion Company Limited is headquartered in Kathmandu and is the only organised participant in Nepal's silver bullion trading market. The company procures raw silver granules, refines them into silver bullion bars and coins, and trades certified 99.99% pure silver products.

Its silver bars are backed by certificates of authenticity, assuring customers of their purity and quality. HBCL is chaired by Bhisma Gautam, who has over two decades of experience in the silver business. Director Suman Gautam also brings extensive experience in investment management.

CARE Ratings Nepal Limited has assigned 'CARE-NP BB+ (Issuer Rating)' to Himalayan Bullion Company Limited. According to the rating agency, entities with this rating are considered to have a moderate risk of default regarding the timely servicing of financial obligations in Nepal.

The company is also preparing to launch an Initial Public Offering (IPO) for the general public. HBCL plans to issue 1.25 million ordinary shares with a face value of Rs. 100 per share, amounting to a total issue size of Rs. 125 million. The company has already formally initiated the IPO process and has appointed Jyoti Capital Limited as the issue and sales manager for the proposed public offering.

title: Nepal’s Wild Tiger Population Reaches 429, Latest National Survey Reveals
content:
Nepal's wild tiger population has risen to 429, up by 74 from the 355 recorded in 2021, according to the latest national survey results announced on World Tiger Day in Chitwan.

The monitoring, conducted by the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation using camera trap technology, shows population growth across four of the country's five tiger habitats: Chitwan leads with 145 tigers (up from 128), followed by Parsa with 71 (up from 41), Banke with 51 (up from 25), and Shuklaphanta with 50 (up from 36). Bardiya National Park was the only location to record a decrease, dropping from 125 to 112 tigers.

Overall, while Nepal's total tiger count continues its steady upward trend, the growth rate slowed to 21 percent over the past four years compared to the 51 percent jump observed between 2018 and 2021.

title: Federation Of Truck Transport Entrepreneurs Seeks Separate Relief fund for Accident Victims Uncovered by Insurance
content:
The Federation Of Truck Transport Entrepreneurs Nepal has urged the government to establish a separate fund to provide relief and treatment support to victims of public vehicle accidents not adequately covered by existing insurance provisions. A federation delegation led by its chairman, Rajendra Bikram Baniya, met Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle on Tuesday and presented the demand, citing gaps in the current insurance framework.

Under the FY 2083/84 budget, insurance provides Rs. 10 Lakhs to the families of accident victims who die and Rs. 3 Lakhs for the medical treatment of injured victims. The federation said actual hospital bills often run into lakhs of rupees, far exceeding this coverage, forcing transport operators, vehicle owners and related associations to bear the additional cost.

The federation has demanded that a dedicated "Injured Relief Fund" be established through legislation, to be operated via transport associations under a separate directive, using contributions collected from operators to support victim's families and fund treatment and rehabilitation for the injured and disabled. It also sought a Value Added Tax exemption on such relief contributions, arguing the funds are used purely for humanitarian purposes and should be included in Schedule 1 of the Value Added Tax Act, 2052.

Minister Wagle said he was positive about creating a separate relief fund to address issues not covered under insurance law, suggesting a directive could be framed with liability resting either solely with operators or shared with the government. However, he said VAT provisions could not be changed immediately within the current fiscal year, asking the federation to approach the ministry roughly five months ahead of the next budget for further discussion.

Separately, the federation drew the government's attention to prolonged disruption at the Tatopani border point, a key Nepal-China trade route blocked by a landslide following heavy rainfall. It said the closure, unresolved for weeks, was costing the country billions of rupees in daily revenue and urged authorities to restore full operations at the crossing immediately.

title: Nepal, WFP Launch Two Reports Showcasing Progress in Food Security and School Meals Programme
content:
The Government of Nepal and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) on Monday unveiled two reports showcasing the country's significant progress in strengthening food security, nutrition, education, climate resilience and social protection through strong government leadership and strategic partnerships.

The two publications, The Journey of the National Mid-Day Meals Programme and WFP's Annual Country Report 2025—highlight Nepal's development achievements and its transition from externally supported initiatives to nationally led systems that have improved the lives of millions, according to a WFP press release.

The reports demonstrate how sustained investment, collaboration and effective government leadership have strengthened national institutions while accelerating progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), WFP said.

"The achievements celebrated today reflect the power of partnership," said Riaz Lodhi, WFP Representative and Country Director in Nepal. "Together with the Government of Nepal, development partners and communities, WFP has helped advance solutions that strengthen food security, improve nutrition, build resilience and support human capital development."

The Journey of the National Mid-Day Meals Programme in Nepal traces the evolution of the country's school meals programme over more than five decades. Launched in 1967 as a small initiative to address classroom hunger, it has grown into one of Nepal's largest social protection programmes, benefiting nearly three million children across all 77 districts and becoming fully funded by the Government of Nepal in 2025.

The report highlights the programme's role in improving school enrolment, attendance, retention and nutrition, while also promoting local food systems through the Home-Grown School Feeding approach, which connects schools with smallholder farmers through cooperatives.

"Finland is proud to support Nepal's education sector through the School Sector Education Plan and Home-Grown School Feeding programme," said Petri Puhakka, Ambassador of Finland to Nepal. "School meals in Nepal are not just about feeding children; they bring together schools, local governments, parents and farmer groups, creating a shared commitment to children's wellbeing and education."

U.S. Embassy Nepal Chargé d'Affaires Scott Urbom said, "The best development investments deliver results far beyond their original purpose. School meals improve education and nutrition while creating reliable markets for Nepali farmers, cooperatives and local businesses. The U.S. Department of Agriculture has proudly partnered with Nepal on this effort since 2005 because a healthier, better educated and more prosperous Nepal is also a stronger partner for the United States, creating new opportunities for trade, investment and cooperation between our countries."

Vice Chair of the National Planning Commission (NPC), Dr. Gunakar Bhatta, stressed that investing in children remains a national priority, noting that strengthening school meals is key to securing Nepal's future prosperity.

He described school meals as a strategic investment that simultaneously advances education, nutrition, agriculture and local economic development, contributing to the country's long-term human capital development.

Minister of Social Development of Sudurpaschim Province, Bel Bahadur Rana Magar, said the nationalisation of the Mid-Day Meals Programme demonstrates what can be achieved through strong government leadership, sustained partnerships and innovation.

He also acknowledged WFP's contribution to strengthening local food systems and creating market opportunities for women and local farmers through stronger school-farmer linkages, while reaffirming the government's commitment to building resilient systems that benefit children, communities and future generations.

The publication further outlines Nepal's plan to expand the programme up to Grade 8 and increase its coverage to around 4.5 million children in the coming years, reinforcing school meals as a key pillar of the country's social protection and human capital development agenda.

Meanwhile, the Annual Country Report 2025 highlights WFP's support to more than 438,000 people through programmes focused on emergency preparedness and response, school meals, nutrition, climate resilience, sustainable livelihoods and food systems transformation. Among its key achievements, the Home-Grown School Feeding initiative benefited more than 208,000 students across Nepal, further strengthening connections between schools, farmers and local markets.

title: Dr. Subash Pyakurel Appointed as Chairman of Nepal's Health Insurance Board
content:
Dr. Subash Pyakurel has been appointed as the Chairman of Nepal's Health Insurance Board. Following his appointment by the Ministry of Health, Dr. Pyakurel officially took the oath of office and secrecy by Minister for Health Nisha Mehta and is set to assume his responsibilities immediately.

Dr. Pyakurel is a prominent healthcare analyst, policy commentator, and social entrepreneur in Nepal. He serves as the founder and CEO of Health Concern Nepal, an organization focused on public health initiatives and healthcare services. Throughout his career, he has been a vocal advocate for public health reform, frequently emphasizing the need for decentralized local healthcare, digital health infrastructure, and the ethical integration of technology in medical services. Additionally, he has been actively involved in discussions surrounding medical education reforms and the creation of equitable healthcare models tailored to strengthen Nepal's overall public health system.

title: Government Forms Talks Committee to Negotiate with Microfinance Victims
content:
Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle has formed a government committee to engage in formal negotiations with protesting microfinance victims. The decision was made through a ministerial level ruling, with Minister Wagle issuing immediate instructions for the newly appointed panel to initiate dialogue with the protesters today.

The negotiation team is led by Mahesh Acharya, a Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Finance. The panel comprises key officials from relevant state institutions, including Joint Secretary Binod Kumar Bhattarai from the Ministry of Law, Joint Secretary Suresh Panthi from the Ministry of Home Affairs, and Executive Director Ramu Paudel from Nepal Rastra Bank. Bolaraj Acharya, an Under Secretary at the Ministry of Finance, serves as the committee's member secretary.

The committee is convening its inaugural meeting at the Ministry of Finance to map out the negotiation framework. Immediately following the preliminary meeting, the panel is scheduled to begin direct discussions with the representatives of the microfinance victims today.

title: Samsung Posts 19-Fold Jump in Q2 Operating Profit Amid Strong AI Demand
content:
South Korean technology giant Samsung Electronics reported a sharp surge in second-quarter earnings on Thursday, driven by robust demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) data centres. The company posted a 19-fold increase in operating profit compared to the same period last year, highlighting the continued momentum in the AI semiconductor market.

Samsung's operating profit for the April–June quarter reached 89.5 trillion won (US$62 billion), representing an increase of more than 1,800% year-on-year. Revenue climbed 130% to 171.5 trillion won, while net profit soared nearly 1,300% to 71.6 trillion won, in line with market expectations.

The strong performance comes despite recent volatility in semiconductor stocks, as investors debate whether the rapid growth driven by AI demand can be sustained. On Wednesday, Samsung shares fell more than 12%, while rival SK hynix dropped nearly 20% after posting earnings that fell short of expectations, although both companies recorded significantly higher profits than a year ago.

Samsung, alongside SK hynix and US-based Micron, remains one of the world's leading producers of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, a critical component powering AI processors used for applications such as chatbots and AI-generated content. The company said its memory business delivered another record-breaking quarter, supported by strong demand for server products.

Looking ahead, Samsung expects server demand to remain robust in the second half of 2026, fuelled by continued investment in AI infrastructure and the broader adoption of agentic AI technologies. Chief Financial Officer Park Soon-cheol also projected that the global memory chip shortage could intensify in 2027 and remain tight through 2028.

Samsung confirmed that its first semiconductor manufacturing facility in Taylor, Texas, remains on schedule to begin operations later this year. Construction of a second plant is expected to commence later in 2026, with mass production targeted for 2030.

Industry analysts noted that the AI boom has also strengthened demand for conventional NAND and DRAM memory chips, further benefiting Samsung's semiconductor business. Recently, the company announced a strategic partnership with US chipmaker Broadcom to supply advanced memory solutions, including HBM, for next-generation AI accelerators. The agreement is estimated to be worth more than US$200 billion through 2030.

Despite speculation about a potential US stock market listing following SK hynix's recent fundraising, Samsung dismissed the possibility, stating that its strong cash generation leaves it with no immediate need to raise additional capital.

The semiconductor industry's rapid growth has also boosted South Korea's economy, prompting the government to support major investments in chip manufacturing. Samsung and SK hynix plan to invest a combined 800 trillion won in developing four advanced semiconductor fabrication plants in Gwangju, although analysts caution that the long-term project may not be completed until after the current semiconductor supercycle has peaked.

title: Super Madi Hydropower Reports 277.68% Rise in Net Profit in Q4; EPS Reaches to Rs. 18.40
content:
Super Madi Hydropower (SMHL)has published its fourth-quarter financial results for FY 2082/83, reporting a strong improvement in profitability, driven primarily by a sharp decline in financing costs alongside higher revenue from power sales.

The company's paid-up capital increased by 5% to Rs. 2.31 Arba, while other equity surged by 219.05% to Rs. 45.14 Crore. Property, plant, and equipment stood at Rs. 8.14 Arba, reflecting a 3.64% decline compared to the previous fiscal year. During the review period, the company made investments worth Rs. 1 Arba, compared to no investment in the corresponding period last year.

Revenue from power sales grew by 18.10% year-on-year to Rs. 1.33 Arba. Meanwhile, finance costs declined significantly by 15.29% to Rs. 46.05 Crore, contributing to a substantial improvement in earnings. Consequently, net profit jumped by 277.68% to Rs. 42.59 Crore. Earnings per share (EPS) rose to Rs. 18.40 from Rs. 5.12, representing a 259.69% increase, while net worth per share edged up by 12.29% to Rs. 119.50.

As of the end of Q4 FY 2082/83, the company's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio stood at 26.36 times, based on a closing market price of Rs. 485 per share.

title: SEBON, Non-Resident Nepali Representatives Discuss Measures to Facilitate Capital Market Participation
content:
The Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) on Wednesday held a discussion and interaction programme with representatives of the Non-Resident Nepali (NRN) community to explore ways to facilitate greater participation of NRNs in Nepal's capital market.

The meeting was attended by SEBON Chairman Dr. Gopal Prasad Bhatta along with senior officials of the board. During the programme, Chairman Bhatta said the discussion marks the beginning of efforts to implement the government's commitment, announced in the national budget, to amend the legal framework allowing Non-Resident Nepalis to participate in Nepal's secondary securities market.

He noted that the initiative has also been incorporated into SEBON's capital market policy and annual programme for the fiscal year 2083/84, with the board set to move forward with the necessary legal and regulatory reforms.

Chairman Bhatta also emphasized that SEBON is ready to facilitate policies that channel the skills, knowledge and capital acquired by Non-Resident Nepalis abroad into Nepal's infrastructure development and broader economic growth.

During the discussion, NRN representatives welcomed the recent initiatives taken by the Government of Nepal and SEBON, stating that they are helping create an enabling environment for Non-Resident Nepalis to invest in Nepal's securities market.

They further shared plans for an investment company jointly established by the Government of Nepal and the NRN community. According to the representatives, the company intends to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO), issuing ordinary shares to Non-Resident Nepalis and Nepalis living abroad, with the proceeds earmarked for investment in Nepal's physical infrastructure projects.

The representatives also said the company plans to mobilise additional capital in the future by issuing project-specific debt instruments, including bonds and debentures, to finance infrastructure investments. They requested SEBON to facilitate the necessary legal and regulatory reforms to support the implementation of these initiatives.

title: NRB to Collect 25 Billion from BFI's for 61 Days
content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has announced that it will collect deposits worth Rs. 25 billion from banks and financial institutions through a bidding process today.

According to a notice published today, the central bank will collect the deposits for a period of 61 days. The bidding will take place on Shrawan 15 (July 31) through the Online Bidding System at 3 Pm.

The interest rate will be decided through the bidding process. The minimum amount for bidding has been set at Rs. 10 crore, while the maximum limit is (In multiples of) 5 Crore, up to the total issue amount. However, institutions can submit multiple bids within the total announced amount.

Only licensed ‘A’, ‘B’, and ‘C’ class banks and financial institutions approved by NRB are allowed to take part in the bidding. The deposits collected will be returned along with interest on Ashoj 14, 2083 (September 30, 2026).

title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah Holds Talks with Madhesh Leaders Over Madhesh Tensions
content:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah has started discussions with leaders of various political parties representing the Madhesh region. The meeting was called to address the current political situation and recent tensions reported in several Madhesh districts, including Sunsari.

The high level meeting is taking place at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers in Singha Durbar. Discussions are primarily focused on reviewing the security situation in affected areas and finding a peaceful resolution through dialogue and mutual agreement.

Prominent Madhesh focused political figures are participating in the talks, including Janamat Party Chairman Dr. C.K. Raut, Loktantrik Samajwadi Party Chairman Mahantha Thakur, senior leader Rajendra Mahato, former Madhesh Province Chief Minister Lalbabu Raut, and Nepal Samajwadi Party Chairman Samim Miya Ansari. Other leaders present include Ram K. Sharma, Prabhu Sah, Amaresh Kumar Singh, Sharat Singh Bhandari, and Jayakanta Raut.

According to government officials, the meeting was organized as part of an effort to resolve recent regional unrest peacefully. The primary goal is to maintain local peace, strengthen social harmony, and guarantee safety and security for all citizens.

title: Muktinath Bikas Bank Signs Agreement with Nagarjun Municipality for Concessional Loans
content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited has signed an agreement with Nagarjun Municipality to provide concessional loans aimed at promoting agriculture, tourism, small and medium enterprises and women entrepreneurship to generate local employment and boost economic activity.

The agreement was signed by Tej Bahadur Giri, Chief of the Agriculture and Inclusive Investment Department at Muktinath Bikas Bank and Sushila Karki, Acting Mayor of Nagarjun municipaltiy, in the presence of bank staff and represantives of the local body.

Under the agreement, eligible entrepreneurs recommended by the municipality can obtain collateral-free loans of up to Rs 200,000 from the bank, depending on the nature of their business. Additionally, eligible borrowers will receive a 100 percent interest subsidy under the municipality's "Concessional Interest Subsidy Procedure, 2080."

On the occasion, the bank reiterated its commitment to contributing to entrepreneurship development, expanding financial access, financial inclusion, and sustainable economic development through collaboration with local governments.

title: Indefinite curfew enforced in some areas in Rajbiraj
content:
The District Administration Office, Saptari, has imposed an indefinite curfew in some sensitive areas of the district headquarters of Rajbiraj Municipality. According to the order issued by Chief District Officer Shyam Krishna Thapa, the curfew was enforced based on the decision of the District Security Committee meeting, effective from 5:00 am today until further notice.

The order states that the curfew has been issued under Section 6 of the Local Administration Act, 2028, and no one is allowed to move around, gather, hold processions, demonstrations, meetings or sit-ins in the designated areas.

According to the administration, the areas where the curfew is in effect include Khandokhola (river) in the east, the Judani-Dhalai road section of the postal highway in the west, Basbitti Chowk of the Rupani road in the north and the Koshi Paschim main canal (Bishnupur Rural Municipality) in the south.

The administration has asked the public to fully comply with the curfew order, stating that curfew order was issued keeping in mind the sensitive situation and to maintain security.

title: Saptakoshi Development Bank Posts 86.18% jump in Net Profit as  Cost of Fund Drops to 3.7
content:
Saptakoshi Development Bank Limited (SAPDBL)has posted a net profit of Rs. 15.04 crore in the Fourth quarter of FY 2082/83, marking an impressive 86.18% rise compared to Rs. 8.08 crore in the same period last fiscal year.

Total deposits increased by 66.48%, reaching Rs. 8.88 arba, while loans and advances rose by 10.41% to Rs. 5.56 arba. Despite these improvements, net interest income dipped slightly by 0.47%, to Rs. 23.34 crores.

Personnel expenses rose slightly by 0.25 percent to Rs 13.69 crore. Meanwhile, Impairment charges on loans and other losses saw a reversal of Rs 19.69 crore in the fourth quarter, compared with a reversal of Rs 4.08 crore in the same quarter last fiscal year. These cost efficiencies contributed to an operating profit of Rs. 24.79 crores, up by 132.05% compared to last fiscal year.

Saptakoshi Development Bank strengthened its capital position, with the capital adequacy ratio increasing to 11.29% from 8.29%. Likewise, net worth per share rose by 30.23% to Rs. 86.71. Non-performing loans (NPL) stood at 6.15%, and the cost of funds decreased to 3.70% from 4.30%.

Earnings per share (EPS) surged to Rs. 18.04 from Rs. 9.69 last year. The company’s Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio at the end of the quarter was 40.48 times, based on a market price of Rs. 730.1 per share.

title: Ten Climbers, Including Five Nepalis, Feared Missing After Avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak
content:
The world renowned climber Nirmal Purja led international expedition team of 10 mountaineers is feared missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak in Pakistan. The Alpine Club of Pakistan received reports on Thursday that an avalanche had struck the team led by Purja, 43, and there has been no communication from the climbers since, the Associated Press (AP) reported quoting club vice-president, Karrar Haidri.

According to the AP, the team consists of five Nepalis, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, a Chinese and next one whose nationality is not confirmed. Meanwhile, Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation Ganesh Paudel has expressed a deep concern to the reports of an avalanche and the loss of contact with Nirmal Purja 'Nims Dai' and fellow Nepali climbers in Pakistan.

Taking to his social site, Minister Paudel stated, "We are in regular contact with the Pakistani authorities and receiving updates on the situation". The Minister has expressed hope for the safe return of all Nepali climbers missing in the avalanche.

title: Sanima Bank Ltd.: A Fourteen - Year Financial Performance Review (Q4 2069/70 - Q4 2082/83)
content:
Background ofSanima Bank Limited(SANIMA)

Sanima Bank Ltd. (SANIMA) is one of the prominent commercial banks in Nepal. It was established in 2004 A.D. Sanima Bank is promoted by a group of prominent and dynamic Non-Resident Nepalese (NRNs) businesspersons. The bank initially commenced operations in 2004 as a National Level Development Bank. Since February 2012, Sanima Bank has been functioning as an "A" Class Commercial Bank with its registered office at 'Alakapuri', Naxal, Kathmandu.

Sanima Bank will start its operations as the 32nd commercial bank of the country from Wednesday Feb 15, 2012 (Falgun 3, 2068 B.S.). Afterward, the bank is operating as one of the most competitive commercial bank. Currently, the bank is serving the nation thorough its 106 full-fledged branches and 28 extension counters spread from all 7 provinces across the country by employing 1,219 staff (As of Annual report 2081/82) nationwide. As of Q4 2082/83, banks total’s assets stood at Rs. 291.21 billion. At the same time, total equity stood at Rs 27.59 billion.

How has SANIMA emerged over the period and role as a national level player in own class? Let’s look at its ups and downs on financial performance during this journey (Q4 2069/70 to Q4 2082/83) of 14 years.

Balance Sheet Analysis

Assets

The overall asset size of SANIMA has increased by 13.25 times, from Rs. 21.97 billion to Rs. 291.21 billion. The proportion of Loans and Advances to Customers to Total Liabilities and Equity remained around the same level at 68.67% in the base year to 67.25% in Q4 2082/83. Below are the major asset indicators over the review period.

1.Cash and Cash Equivalents

Cash and cash equivalents increased from Rs. 1.68 billion to Rs. 18.96 billion. Holding cash and cash equivalents above regulatory requirement is generally not considered efficient for banks. In this regard, SANIMA has an excess position due to higher liquidity in the market.

2.Loans and Advances to Customers

The bank has remarkably expanded its core lending business. Loans and advances increased by 12.98 times, from Rs. 15.09 billion as of Q4 2069/70 to Rs. 195.88 billion by Q4 2082/83. Over the fourteen - year period, the bank achieved remarkable growth in business expansion.

3.Property and Equipment

Property and Equipment initially stood at Rs. 46.94 crore and showed an increasing trend and reached Rs. 1.34 billion in Q4 2082/83. This category may also include certain non-banking properties.

4.Total Assets

Total assets increased with higher growth during the initial years. Although the growth rate slowed in recent years, assets continued to grow steadily. Overall, SANIMA's asset base expanded by 13.25 times, increasing from Rs. 21.97 billion in Q4 2069/70 to Rs. 291.21 billion in Q4 2082/83.

Liabilities

Total liabilities (excluding equity) stood at Rs. 19.54 billion in Q4 2069/70. They increased by 13.49 times, reaching Rs. 263.62 billion by Q4 2082/83. Deposits from customers, the bank's core liability, grew at a median annual growth rate of 13.57%, increasing from Rs. 17.78 billion to Rs. 249.11 billion. Meanwhile, total liabilities and equity combined increased from Rs. 21.97 billion to Rs. 291.21 billion. The major liability trends are discussed below.

1.Deposits from Customers

Deposits from customers increased at a median annual growth rate of 13.57%. Within total liabilities (excluding equity), deposits accounted for 91% of total liabilities in Q4 2069/70, increased to 95% by Q4 2082/83. This indicates that the bank remains highly dependent on customer deposits and may need to diversify its funding sources by utilizing other financial instruments.

2.Other Liabilities

Other liabilities are steadily increasing throughout the review period. From Q4 2069/70 to Q4 2082/83, they increased by 14.10 times. This category reached its highest level in recent review period, which is in increasing trend.

3.Total Liabilities

Total liabilities followed a pattern similar to customer deposits, recording a median annual growth rate of 16.73%. Since deposits constitute the largest portion of liabilities, total liabilities closely tracked deposit growth.

4.Equity Analysis

Total equity of SANIMA increased at a median annual growth rate of 13.28%. During the same period, share capital grew at a median annual rate of 10%, while reserves increased at a median annual rate of 23.85%.

Profit and Loss Analysis

1.Interest Income and Expenses

Interest income and interest expense represent the bank's core revenue-generating activities and the cost of funding those assets, respectively. Interest income declined after reaching its peak of Rs. 21.61 billion in Q4 2079/80. Thereafter, both interest income and interest expense decreased steadily. By Q4 2082/83, interest income had fallen to Rs. 16.60 billion.

During the declining interest rate environment, SANIMA’s net interest income continued to increase. Although the interest spread rate narrowed, the bank appeared to have successfully expanded its lending business.

2.Net Fees and Commission Income

Another positive aspect of SANIMA is the steady growth in its net fees and commission income. SANIMA earned Rs. 1.49 billion in Q4 2082/83, representing a significant increasement of 63.99 times over review period.

3.Operating Profit and Net Profit

Operating profit reflects the bank's profitability before taxation and provisioning, while distributable net profit represents earnings attributable to shareholders.

SANIMA recorded its highest-ever net profit of Rs. 3.55 billion in Q4 2082/83. Overall, the bank has maintained a steady growth trend in net profits. Over the review period, the bank has achieved media growth rate of 30.27 percent in net profits.

Interest expense remains the bank's largest expense and is considered the primary direct cost in the banking industry. This expense has shown a declining trend. However, persistently lower interest expenses may make it more challenging for the bank to retain depositors' funds. Other operating expenses have remained at a moderate level.

Personnel expense of SANIMA is in increasing trend. Tax liability is directly related to profit. Rising profit increases tax liability of SANIMA.

Trends in Key Performance Indicators

Earnings Metrics

Earnings Per Share (EPS)

title: Nepal Rastra Bank Takes Action Against Three Commercial Banks
content:
Nepal’s central bank, Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), has taken supervisory action against three major commercial banks, Prabhu Bank, Rastriya Banijya Bank, and Agriculture Development Bank, for failing to comply with regulatory standards and financial guidelines. As part of these enforcement actions, NRB also imposed a cash fine of Rs 500,000 on Prabhu Bank’s former Chief Executive Officer, Ashok Sherchan.

According to the central bank's Bank Supervision Department, the action against Prabhu Bank and its executive leadership stems from multiple compliance failures. Inspections revealed that the bank failed to adhere to mandatory loan classification rules, did not set aside sufficient funds for potential loan losses, and submitted loan records to the central bank that did not match the data in its internal core banking system. Consequently, the central bank fined Sherchan under Section 100(2)(c) of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058.

Meanwhile, state-owned Rastriya Banijya Bank was issued a formal caution under Section 100(1)(a) of the NRB Act after it failed to freeze specified bank accounts within required timelines, violating the updated bank account management regulations. Additionally, Agriculture Development Bank was required to sign a written commitment to undertake corrective measures after supervisory audits identified operational deficiencies.

The regulatory body stated that these supervisory actions aim to strengthen institutional governance, maintain transparency in financial reporting, and ensure strict compliance across Nepal's banking sector.

title: Mountaineering Legend Nirmal Purja Dies in Broad Peak Avalanche; Elite Exped Confirms Tragic Loss
content:
World-record-holding Nepali mountaineer Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja has died in an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak (8,047m), his expedition company Elite Exped confirmed on Saturday.

Purja was among three Nepali climbers who lost their lives in the tragic avalanche. His trusted climbing companions, Purba Bahadur Gurung (Yukta) and Nima Sherpa, also died during the expedition.

In a statement shared on social media, Elite Exped expressed profound grief, describing Purja as an extraordinary leader who inspired millions through his courage, humility, and determination. The company said his legacy would continue to inspire future generations and extended heartfelt condolences to the families of all those who lost their lives.

The company also thanked the search and rescue teams for their efforts and requested the public to respect the privacy of the bereaved families. It added that no further comments would be made beyond information confirmed by the relevant authorities.

The bodies were located during a drone search near Camp 1 before ground rescuers successfully recovered and identified them despite challenging weather and terrain.

A former British Gurkha soldier, Purja achieved global recognition in 2019 after setting a world record by climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-meter peaks in just 6 months and 6 days. His remarkable achievement was featured in the acclaimed Netflix documentary "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible."

title: Miteri Development Bank Ltd. (MDB): A Fourteen - Year Financial Performance Review (Q4 2069/70 - Q4 2082/83)
content:
Background of Miteri Development Bank Ltd. (MDB)

Miteri Development Bank (MDB) commenced operations on 13 October 2006. This is a regional -level class ‘B’ bank. Its head office is located at Mahendrapath, Dharan – 5, Sunsari district, Koshi Province. The bank provides development banking products and services in the eastern region of Nepal. It has been serving people across three districts while contributing to society and the nation to the best of its capacity.

Here, we examine its financial performance over the past fourteen fiscal years based on fourth-quarter unaudited reports. In this article, we will evaluate from fiscal year 2069/70 to 2082/83. How the regional level development bank performing?

Balance Sheet Analysis

Assets

The overall asset size of MDB has increased by 9.29 times, from Rs. 1.15 billion to Rs. 10.72 billion. The proportion of Loans and Advances to Customers to Total Liabilities and Equity decreased from 85.66% in the base year to 82.54% in Q4 2082/83. Below are the major asset indicators over the review period.

1.Cash and Cash Equivalents

Cash and cash equivalents have fluctuated over the period. This item stood at Rs. 27.79 crore in the latest review period, compared with Rs. 22.19 crore in the base year. Holding cash and cash equivalents above the regulatory requirement is generally not considered efficient for banks. In this regard, MDB maintains moderate liquidity position.

2.Loans and Advances to Customers

The bank has remarkably expanded its core lending business. Loans and advances increased by 7.93 times, from Rs. 84.36 crore as of Q4 2069/70 to Rs. 6.69 billion by Q4 2082/83. Over the fourteen - year period, the bank achieved remarkable growth in business expansion based on the bank’s size and permitted area for operation.

3.Property and Equipment

Property and equipment initially stood at Rs. 87.95 lakh and showed an increasing trend and reached Rs. 5.51 crore as of Q4 2082/83. it peaked highest in Q4 2079/80 reached Rs. 5.58 crore. This category may also include certain non-banking properties.

4.Total Assets

Total assets increased at a higher growth rate during the initial years. Although the growth rate slowed in recent years, assets continued to grow steadily. Overall, MDB's asset base expanded by 9.29 times, increasing from Rs. 1.15 billion in Q4 2069/70 to Rs. 10.72 billion in Q4 2082/83.

Liabilities

Total liabilities (excluding equity) stood at Rs. 1 billion in Q4 2069/70. They increased by 8.97 times, reaching Rs. 8.98 billion by Q4 2082/83. Deposits from customers, the bank's core liability, grew at a median annual growth rate of 18.14%, decrease from Rs. 9.88 billion to Rs. 8.85 billion. Meanwhile, total liabilities and equity combined increased from Rs. 1.15 billion to Rs. 10.72 billion. The major liability trends are discussed below.

1.Deposits from Customers

Deposits from customers increased at a median annual growth rate of 18.14%. Within total liabilities (excluding equity), deposits accounted for 98.70% in Q4 2069/70, decreased marginally to 98.59% by Q4 2082/83. This indicates that the bank remains highly dependent on customer deposits and may need to diversify its funding sources by utilizing other financial instruments.

2.Other Liabilities

Other liabilities increased steadily throughout the review period. From Q4 2069/70 to Q4 2082/83, they increased from Rs. 1.20 crore to Rs. 7.88 crore. This category reached its highest level of Rs. 12.76 crores in Q4 2076/77.

3.Total Liabilities

Total liabilities followed a pattern like customer deposits, recording a median annual growth rate of 18.94%. Since deposits constitute the largest portion of liabilities, total liabilities closely tracked deposit growth.

4.Equity Analysis

Total equity of MDB increased at a median annual growth rate of 17.19%. During the same period, share capital grew at a median annual rate of 16%, while reserves increased at a median annual rate of 16.50%.

Profit and Loss Analysis

1.Interest Income and Expenses

Interest income and interest expense represent the bank's core revenue-generating activities and the cost of funding those assets, respectively. Interest income declined after reaching its peak of Rs. 97.65 crore in Q4 2079/80. Thereafter, both interest income and interest expense decreased steadily. By Q4 2082/83, interest income had fallen to Rs. 67.41 crore.

During the declining interest rate environment, MDB median growth of interest income and expense didn’t differ significantly. On the positive side, net interest income continued to increase. The interest spread rate narrowed, the bank may affect negatively.

2.Net Fees and Commission Income

Another positive aspect of MDB is the steady growth in its net fees and commission income. MDB earned Rs. 3.83 crore in Q4 2082/83, representing an increase of approximately 18 times over the review period.

3.Operating Profit and Net Profit

Operating profit reflects the bank's profitability before taxation and provisioning, while distributable net profit represents earnings attributable to shareholders.

MDB’s net profit of seemed as stagnated for growth. After reaching the highest peak on Rs. 16.73 crore in 76/77 afterward, growth either in negative or lower growth. MDB earned Rs. 14.12 crore in Q4 2082/83.

4.Expenses

Interest expense remains the bank's largest expense and is considered the primary direct cost in the banking industry. This expense has shown a declining trend. However, persistently lower interest expenses may make it more challenging for the bank to retain depositors' funds. Other operating expenses have remained at a moderate level.

Trends in Key Performance Indicators

Earnings Per Share (EPS)

Till recent year, the bank has maintained EPS above Rs. 10. A sharp decline from Rs. 46.02 in 2072/73 to Rs. 22.59 in 2074/75 represents the higher decline in earnings performance during the review period.

Q4 2082/83 closed with Distributable EPS of Rs. 12.73, indicating that profitability has substantially improved compared to the post-pandemic years.

FY2082/83 recorded 8.1%, The ratio remained low and relatively stable for this year. Although current returns remain stable there is fear of declining in coming year if bank couldn’t expand business.

title: Tea exports to India decline through Kakarvitta point
content:
Exports of Nepali tea to India through the eastern border point at Kakarvitta in Jhapa have declined. According to the Kakarvitta Customs Office, both the volume and value of tea exports declined during the last fiscal year 2082/83 BS compared to the previous fiscal year.

Customs Office statistics indicate that Nepal exported 13,045 metric tons of tea worth Rs 3.53 billion to India in fiscal year 2082/83 BS, down from 15,311 metric tons worth Rs 4.17 billion in fiscal year 2081/82 BS. Along with the decline in the export volume, tea export earnings also fell by Rs 639.69 million. According to Chief Customs Administrator Shivlal Neupane, tea is the second-largest export commodity, after cardamom, shipped through the Karkarvitta border point.

Neupane said that since India is the primary market for Nepali tea, exports have been affected by price fluctuations in the Indian market, non-tariff barriers related to quality testing, and changes in production and pricing driven by international market demand.

A significant portion of CTC and orthodox tea produced in Nepal is supplied to the Indian market via the Karkarvitta point. The decline in exports is expected to adversely affect tea farmers, industrialists and suppliers, while also widening the country's trade deficit.

title: Ridi Power Shuts Down 9.9 MW Iwa Khola Hydropower Project After Flood Damage to Pipeline Infrastructure
content:
Ridi Power Company Limited has announced the temporary shutdown of its 9.9 MW Iwa Khola Hydropower Project in Panchthar district after severe flood and landslide damage rendered the project's pipeline unsafe for operation.

According to the company, continuous heavy rainfall since Jestha triggered floods and landslides that caused significant riverbank erosion around the project's headrace pipeline. The erosion damaged critical support structures, including anchor blocks, pipe supports, and other civil infrastructure.

The company stated that persistent rainfall also caused erosion beneath the pipeline, creating excessive pressure that led to multiple pipe bursts and cracks at various locations.

Following the damage, Ridi Power carried out repair works and conducted phased testing in an effort to resume electricity generation. However, during the testing process, additional damage was detected at several points along the pipeline.

After conducting a detailed technical assessment, the company concluded that routine repairs or welding alone would not be sufficient to restore the project safely, necessitating more extensive rehabilitation work.

As a result, the Iwa Khola Hydropower Project has remained under plant shutdown since Ashadh 26 to facilitate permanent repair and technical restoration.

Ridi Power said that comprehensive technical inspections and permanent repair works are currently underway. The company added that it will issue another formal notice to inform stakeholders once the exact date and time for the project's recommissioning have been confirmed.

This suspension on share transactions will remain in effect until the merger is fully finalized and approved during the upcoming annual general meetings of both organizations.

title: Nepal Oil Corporation Raises Fuel Prices; Petrol Hits Rs. 200 Per Liter in Kathmandu
content:
The Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) has increased the prices of petroleum products, with the revised rates set to take effect from 12:01 am tonight.

According to the corporation, the price of petrol has been increased by Rs. 3 per liter, while diesel and kerosene have each been raised by Rs. 5 per liter. The price of domestic aviation fuel has also been increased by Rs. 20 per liter, while international aviation fuel has been raised by USD 131 per kiloliter.

Despite the latest increase in retail fuel prices, NOC stated that it is still projected to incur a fortnightly loss of approximately Rs. 1.49 billion after adjusting petroleum product prices, according to a statement issued on Monday.

title: IPPAN Urges Hydropower Developers to Issue Local Shares at Face Value of Rs. 100
content:
TheIndependent Power Producers' Association, Nepal(IPPAN) has urged all hydropower promoter companies to continue issuing shares to project-affected local communities at the face value of Rs. 100 per share, in line with existing legal provisions.

In a statement issued on Monday, IPPAN expressed serious concern over discussions by some hydropower developers about issuing local shares at a premium price due to delays in the initial public offering (IPO) approval process for certain hydropower projects.

According to IPPAN PresidentMohan Kumar Dangi, prolonged delays in the IPO issuance process have prompted some companies to consider alternative pricing for shares allocated to residents directly affected by hydropower projects. However, the association emphasized that such a move would contradict the spirit of the existing legal framework and could undermine the objectives of local share allocation.

Under the Securities Registration and Issue Regulations, 2073 (2017), hydropower companies are required to allocate 10 percent of their issued shares to project-affected local communities. IPPAN has called on all its member companies to ensure that these shares continue to be offered at their face value of Rs. 100 per share.

The association stressed that hydropower development is not merely an investment opportunity but also a long-term development partnership built on trust, cooperation, and shared ownership with local communities.

IPPAN noted that the provision for allocating shares to residents was introduced to recognize the contributions and sacrifices of communities that provide land for projects, bear environmental and social impacts, endure construction-related inconveniences, and support the successful implementation of hydropower projects.

The association warned that issuing local shares at a premium price would limit the participation of affected communities, weaken their sense of ownership, and potentially damage the trust that has been built over the years between project developers and residents.

According to IPPAN, providing shares at face value enables local communities to become genuine stakeholders in hydropower projects, strengthens their ownership, and helps minimize social disputes and project-related obstacles during construction and operation. The association believes this approach also fosters stronger local cooperation, facilitates timely project completion, and creates long-term economic benefits for residents through increased financial participation, local development, and social harmony.

IPPAN further urged the Government of Nepal, relevant regulatory authorities, and all hydropower developers to prioritize the interests of project-affected communities, ensure the long-term sustainability of hydropower projects, and preserve the healthy relationship between the private sector and local communities by maintaining the policy of issuing local shares at the face value of Rs. 100 per share.

The association also called on the government and regulatory agencies to simplify, improve transparency, and expedite the regulatory process related to IPO approvals. It stated that delays in the share issuance process have created significant challenges for hydropower projects and urged authorities to establish a more efficient and time-bound approval mechanism to ensure timely public offerings.

title: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) Set to Become Legal Money in Nepal
content:
Nepal is taking a major step toward recognizing digital money issued by its central bank, while maintaining a strict stance against private cryptocurrencies. A proposed amendment bill to the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058 seeks to give official legal status to Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), classifying it alongside traditional paper notes and physical coins.

The scope and legal boundaries of digital money were discussed during a clause-by-clause review of the bill by the Finance Committee of the House of Representatives. Officials clarified that the term "digital currency" in the new law applies strictly to money issued, regulated, and backed by Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the nation's central bank. In contrast, privately issued digital assets, such as cryptocurrencies and virtual currencies, will not be recognized as official currency or legal money.

Addressing lawmakers, NRB Executive Director Deergha Rawal explained that incorporating digital currency into the Act specifically enables the launch and management of a central bank digital currency. He noted that private cryptocurrencies do not belong in the central banking law, as regulatory concerns surrounding them are already covered under anti-money laundering legislation.

Finance Secretary Dr. Ghanashyam Upadhyay emphasized the distinction between digital currency and digital banking, advising that they should not be conflated. Because digital currency naturally functions within its own operational framework, he noted that adding a separate operational system definition is unnecessary. To ensure clarity, he suggested defining digital currency simply as any digital money issued or designated by the central bank, which maintains sole authority over official currency.

Under the proposed amendment to Section 2 of the Act, the definition of "currency" will be officially expanded. While the current law recognizes only paper banknotes and metal coins, the updated provision will define currency to include bank notes in active circulation, coins, and digital currency issued directly by the central bank. Proposers of the amendment further recommended explicit language stating that any private virtual currency or cryptocurrency remains strictly excluded from being considered lawful money under the Act.

title: Former Finance Minister Khanal Calls for Major Policy Reforms to Revive Nepal's MSMEs
content:
Former Finance Minister Rameshore Khanal has stressed the need for sweeping reforms in insurance, lending, and policy frameworks to revive Nepal's micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), many of which continue to struggle in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Speaking at a policy discussion programme organized by the Society of Economic Journalists Nepal (SEJON), the Nepal Insurance Authority, and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) during the release of the study report Risk Management in Nepal's MSMEs, Khanal said comprehensive policy reforms are essential to safeguard and promote businesses facing ongoing economic challenges.

He noted that while MSMEs are a vital pillar of Nepal's economy, the sector has weakened due to inadequate risk management mechanisms and limited access to finance.

Khanal also proposed innovative changes to agricultural insurance schemes, suggesting that the government should initially bear 100 percent of insurance premiums for low-income farmers and recover their contribution only after compensation is paid. He argued that despite the government's subsidy of up to 75 percent on insurance premiums, many farmers have been unable to fully benefit from the programme.

Referring to the newly released report, Khanal said only around 10 percent of Nepal's nearly 900,000 MSMEs have insurance coverage, leaving the remaining 90 percent exposed to various risks. He added that although sectors such as tourism and construction are gradually recovering from the pandemic, MSMEs remain under severe financial pressure, contributing to rising bad loans and growing non-performing assets in banks and financial institutions.

On the occasion, Kalpana Shrestha, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, emphasized the need to expand insurance coverage by integrating government programmes designed to support MSMEs.

She said that nearly half of Nepal's approximately 923,000 MSMEs operate in the informal sector and remain outside the insurance system, limiting overall insurance penetration to around 10 percent. To address this gap, she highlighted government initiatives such as startup loans, MEDPA programmes, production-based incentives, and the National Enterprise Facility aimed at promoting entrepreneurship.

Kyoko Yokosuka, Resident Representative of UNDP Nepal, said MSMEs form the backbone of Nepal's economy but are among the most vulnerable to growing climate and economic risks.

She noted that through its Insurance and Risk Finance Facility, UNDP is working with 39 countries, including Nepal, to strengthen financial resilience against climate- and disaster-related risks, reaffirming the organization's commitment to expanding affordable and appropriate insurance solutions for MSMEs.

Meanwhile, Sushildev Subedi, Executive Director of the Nepal Insurance Authority, said Nepal's insurance system must become more inclusive, modern, and effective to better protect MSMEs from emerging risks.

He added that MSMEs are particularly vulnerable to natural disasters, climate change, financial shocks, cyber threats, and public health emergencies, making effective risk management essential for their long-term sustainability.

title: National Agriculture Policy 2083  Launched
content:
The Ministry of Agriculture, Forest, and Environment has officially issued the National Agriculture Policy 2083, aiming to transform Nepal’s farming sector into a modern, commercial, competitive, and self-reliant industry. Prepared in alignment with the country's federal governance system, the policy focuses on achieving food security and food sovereignty, raising farmers' incomes, increasing domestic agricultural production, substituting imports, and promoting farm exports.

Speaking on the launch of the policy, Minister for Agriculture, Forest, and Environment Gita Chaudhary stated that the primary objective of the new policy is to overcome existing sectoral challenges and establish a sustainable, production-focused agricultural system. The policy outlines specific measures to tackle major issues such as land fragmentation, the growth of uncultivated land, lack of irrigation and storage facilities, youth migration, the impacts of climate change, low productivity, and increasing reliance on imported food.

To achieve its goals, the policy establishes measures to gain self-reliance in basic food items, promote agricultural commercialization and industrial development, and expand into international markets by branding local farm products. It also stresses the importance of protecting biodiversity, developing environment-friendly farming systems, and incorporating digital technology, local knowledge, and innovation into agricultural practices.

Additionally, the policy prioritizes boosting farm productivity, promoting inclusive machinery use, conserving land, expanding agricultural research, and providing practical support to farmers through minimum support prices, subsidized farm loans, crop and livestock insurance, and improved food safety and nutrition. It further encourages investment from the private sector and cooperatives, soil health management, climate adaptation, stronger agricultural data collection, and efforts to establish farming as a respected profession.

According to the ministry, effective execution of the policy will rely on strong coordination among federal, provincial, and local governments, along with necessary legal structures, sufficient financial funding, private sector involvement, and regular monitoring and evaluation. The ministry expects that the successful implementation of the National Agriculture Policy 2083 will significantly contribute to food self-sufficiency, job creation, import reduction, export growth, and overall national economic prosperity.
