title: Bagmati Province Chief Minister Indra Bahadur Baniya Resigns
content:
Indra Bahadur Baniya, the Chief Minister of Bagmati Province, announced his resignation from the position.

Addressing the beginning of today's meeting at the Bagmati Provincial Assembly, Baniya shared that he stepped down to pave the way for the formation of a new government in light of recent political developments.

He stated that he would formally submit his resignation letter to the Provincial Head shortly. During his address, Baniya highlighted key achievements from his term in office, including reducing the province’s running costs by capping the number of ministries at eight. He also highlighted public welfare initiatives such as constructing housing for poor families, rebuilding damaged infrastructure, and making the transport sector digital and modern.

title: Government, Foreign Employment Agencies Agree to Address 15 Demands Within 45 Days
content:
The dispute between foreign employment agencies and the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security has been resolved following an agreement to address the agencies’ 15-point demands within 45 days.

Following the agreement, foreign employment businesses have suspended all protest programs and decided to resume their regular operations from tomorrow.

According to Hari Dangi, General Secretary of the Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies, agencies will reopen their offices and resume services after reaching an understanding with the ministry.

The agencies had previously announced the closure of their offices and suspension of worker recruitment and deployment, citing the government’s failure to address their demands.

Key Demands to Be AddressedThe agencies had been demanding reforms in areas including the determination of service charges and withdrawal of actions taken against recruitment agencies by the Department of Foreign Employment.

Under the agreement, the ministry and the association have agreed to address policy-related demands through amendments to the Foreign Employment Act and related regulations.

The association had been conducting protests and awareness programs since August 7 (Shrawan 22), putting forward a 15-point set of demands.

The agreement is expected to bring an end to the ongoing disruption in foreign employment services and allow recruitment agencies to resume the regular processing and deployment of Nepali workers for overseas employment.

title: NAIMA Nepal Mobility Expo 2026 Concludes with Over 180,000 Visitors and 53 New Product Launches
content:
The NAIMA Nepal Mobility Expo 2026 concluded successfully on Sunday, August 16, attracting more than 180,000 visitors over its six-day run at Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu. Organized by the Nepal Automobile Importers and Manufacturers Association (NAIMA), the second edition of the mobility expo drew significantly more visitors than the organizer’s initial target of 150,000.

The expo officially opened on August 11 amid a grand ceremony and witnessed a steady rise in public interest throughout its six-day schedule. According to NAIMA, more than 29,000 visitors attended on the opening day, followed by 26,000 on the second day, 22,000 on the third, 31,000 on the fourth, and more than 42,000 on Saturday, the fifth day. On the closing day alone, more than 30,000 visitors visited the expo.

NAIMA President Ritu Singh Vaidya said the participation of more than 55 brands, over 180,000 visitors, and the launch of 53 new products were among the expo’s major achievements. She described the event as a collective success for Nepal’s entire mobility industry rather than the achievement of any individual or organization.

“This expo is not the success of any one person or institution; it is the collective success of Nepal’s entire mobility industry,” Vaidya said, thanking all participating companies and stakeholders. She said the expo was designed not only to showcase new vehicles and technologies but also to promote knowledge, learning and interaction within the mobility sector.

“This is not the end, but the beginning,” Vaidya said, adding that NAIMA aims to make future editions bigger, better and stronger. Organizers said customer inquiries and vehicle bookings during the expo also exceeded expectations, reflecting strong consumer interest in Nepal’s automobile and mobility market.

Auto Show Planning Committee Chair Gaurav Sharda said the number of visitors was higher than anticipated and that inquiries and bookings also surpassed initial expectations. NAIMA Board Member Cabinet Shrestha described the large turnout as a positive development for Nepal’s automobile industry.

“NAIMA Expo has been successful in every respect. This is encouraging for the entire automobile industry,” he said. Similarly, NAIMA Strategy and Membership Affairs Committee Chair Aakash Golchha described the expo as a “superhit.” The expo went beyond vehicle displays, featuring a series of discussions, dialogues and interactive sessions focused on emerging issues in Nepal’s mobility sector.

The NAIMA Mobility Dialogue was held on the closing day, featuring House of Representatives member Vidushi Rana, NAIMA Board Member and Padma Jyoti Group Chairperson Saurabh Jyoti, Padma Kanya Campus Assistant Professor Bhagwati Sedain and Thapathali Engineering Campus Assistant Professor Lochan Kendra Devkota.

Other discussions during the expo covered topics including artificial intelligence and automotive technology, battery recycling, ethanol blending, vehicle financing and insurance, the present and future of mobility, investment and foreign direct investment, among others.

According to NAIMA, the second edition of the expo focused on promoting a sustainable, green, and technology-friendly transportation system in Nepal. The event brought together domestic and multinational vehicle manufacturers and importers, as well as banks, insurance companies, technology and charging companies, educational institutions, ride-sharing platforms, and organizations working in health and safety, which also participated and supported the expo.

NAIMA Executive Director Raj Kumar Dulal said the organizers emphasized learning, collaboration, and demand-driven management alongside the large-scale vehicle exhibition. He said visitor satisfaction was the key indicator of the expo’s success. The turnout of more than 180,000 visitors and the strong interest in newly launched products have demonstrated continued consumer enthusiasm for Nepal’s automobile and mobility sector.

With more than 55 brands participating and 53 new products unveiled, the NAIMA Nepal Mobility Expo 2026 has emerged as a major platform for introducing new vehicles, technologies, and mobility solutions, while creating opportunities for consumers, businesses, and industry stakeholders to engage directly.

title: Muktinath Bikas Bank Customers to Get Up to 20% Discount at Bar Peepal Resort
content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has partnered with Bar Peepal Resort Pokhara to provide special discounts to its customers.

Customers can receive 10% to 20% discounts on food, accommodation, and other services by using the bank’s valid debit/privilege card or paying through mobile banking.

Groups of more than six people will also receive complimentary accommodation and breakfast, lunch, and dinner for one person. The bank has also introduced an Auto Loan at 0% premium over the base rate.

title: NIC Asia Bank’s “NIC Asia Debenture 2083/84” to Mature on Bhadra 10
content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited has announced that its debenture issue titled“NIC Asia Debenture 2083/84”is set to mature after Bhadra 10, 2083.

The bank had issued 1,943,698 units of debentures with a face value of Rs. 1,000 per unit, carrying a fixed interest rate of 10.25 percent and a maturity period of seven years.

The debentures were subsequently listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange Limited (NEPSE) following a listing agreement signed between NEPSE and the bank on Mangsir 18, 2076.

As the debentures will mature after Bhadra 10, 2083, the bank has requested the concerned authorities to initiate necessary procedures in accordance with the listing agreement and regulatory provisions.

title: Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Customers to Get Up to 20% Discount on Health, Hospitality Services
content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank has partnered with several organizations in the healthcare, hospitality, food and beverage, and retail sectors to provide special discounts to customers using its debit cards, credit cards, and mobile banking services.

Discounts of up to 20% are available on selected health and laboratory services, while hospitality, dining, and retail services offer discounts of up to 15%.

The bank said the partnerships aim to provide direct benefits to customers. It has also recently launched a digital hub with a coffee lounge in Gyaneshwor, Kathmandu.

title: Reminder! Last Trading Day to Secure Dividend of Kumari Equity Fund, Kumari Dhanabriddhi Yojana, and Kumari Sabal Yojana
content:
Today is the last day to grab the dividend proposed by"Kumari Equity Fund (KEF)", "Kumari Dhanabriddhi Yojana (KDBY) and "Kumari Sabal Yojana (KSY)".

The 85th meeting of the board of directors of Kumari Capital Limited (KCL) held on Shrawan 21 has decided to distribute a 10% dividend (including tax) worth Rs. 10 Crore to Kumari Equity Fund (KEF), 10% dividend (including tax) worth Rs. 12.25 Crore to Kumari Dhanabriddhi Yojana (KDBY) and a 2.90% cash dividend (including tax) worth 2.15 Crores to the unitholders of Kumari Sabal Yojana (KSY) for the fiscal year 2081/82.

"Kumari Equity Fund (KEF)", "Kumari Dhanabriddhi Yojana (KDBY) and "Kumari Sabal Yojana (KSY)" are closed-end mutual funds with a 10-year maturity period. These funds are sponsored by Kumari Bank Limited and managed by Kumari Capital Limited.

For the month of Ashadh, KEF's Net Asset Value (NAV) is reported at Rs. 11.44. Similarly, the NAV of KDBY stands at Rs. 12.26, and the NAV of KSY is 10.29.

The book closure date is Bhadra 04. Thus, unit holders who maintained their holdings until the 3rd Bhadra are entitled to the dividend payout.

title: Mid Solu Hydropower Announces Conclusion of Lock-in Period for Promoters Local Residents of the Project Affected Area And Employees Shares on Ashwin 10
content:
Mid Solu Hydropower Company Limited (MSHL)published a notice regarding the expiration of the lock-in period of its promoters, residents of the project-affected area, and employees' shares, which will expire on 10th Ashwin, 2083.

According to the recent guidelines issued by the Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON), Mid Solu Hydropower Company Limited (MSHL) has officially notified its investors and stakeholders of the conclusion of the lock-in period for the shares held by its promoters and employee shares. In the next month of the 10th Ashwin, 2083, the lock-in period will end.

MSHL now has 8,606,600 units of shares listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE). Within the total of 8,606,600 units of shares, the promoters held 68,85,280 units, the residents of the project-affected area held 8,60,660 units, and the employees held 17,213 units of shares, all subject to a lock-in period since the IPO allotment two years ago.

As outlined in the official notice, the shares held by the Board of Directors and employees at higher management won't be tradable after the lock-in period.

MSHL closed at Rs. 586.00.

title: NADA Auto Show 2026 to Feature 200+ Stalls and 50th Anniversary Special Attractions
content:
The 18th edition of the NADA Auto Show 2026 is set to take place at Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, from Bhadra 9 to 14 as a special Golden Jubilee Edition marking the 50th anniversary of the NADA Automobiles Association of Nepal. The six-day exhibition is presented by HP Lubricants as the title sponsor and aims to showcase the latest developments, products and technologies shaping Nepal’s automobile and mobility industry.

Spread across around 300,000 square feet, the expo will feature more than 200 stalls, including 23 passenger vehicle brands, 17 light commercial vehicle brands, 13 two-wheeler brands, 10 financial and insurance service providers, and around 70 automotive parts, accessories, tyre, lubricant and garage-equipment exhibitors.

Major attractions will include new vehicle launches, the G1 Humanoid Robot and Go2 Quadruped Robot, a Made in Nepal/Made for Nepal Pavilion, and symposiums focusing on smart mobility, sustainable automotive development and connectivity. The event will also provide dedicated zones for vehicles, two-wheelers, financial services and automotive components.

Visitors will have access to advance ticket booking through Khalti, parking facilities, traffic information, medical and emergency services, CCTV surveillance, fire safety arrangements, media facilities, cafeterias and wheelchair-friendly infrastructure. NADA expects around 200,000 visitors during the six-day event.

title: Unveiling Q4 2082/83: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks and Key Financial Insights
content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the fourth quarter of FY 2082/83, offering a fresh look into their performance during the twelve months. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.

In Q4 FY 2082/83, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led Nepal’s commercial banks with the highest net profit of Rs. 7.90 Arba, followed by Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) with Rs. 7.38 Arba and Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) with Rs. 6.22 Arba. Nabil Bank’s profit increased by 33.45% compared to Rs. 5.92 Arba in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.

Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) recorded the highest profit growth among the commercial banks, with a staggering 1133.33% increase, rising to Rs. 1.48 Arba from Rs. 0.12 Arba. Kumari Bank Limited followed with a strong 307.73% growth, while Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) posted a 63.28% increase.

On the other hand, Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) recorded the sharpest decline in net profit, dropping by 127.59% to a loss of Rs. 0.24 Arba from a profit of Rs. 0.87 Arba. Similarly, NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw its net profit decline by 104.65% year-on-year, reporting a profit of Rs. 0.18 Arba compared to a loss of Rs. 3.87 Arba in the previous year.

Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 32.05 Arba. Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) and Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) follow with Rs. 26.78 Arba and Rs. 26.23 Arba, respectively.

Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba, followed by Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) at Rs. 11.33 Arba and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 13.72 Arba. The combined paid-up capital of the 20 commercial banks stands at Rs. 411.17 Arba, with an average of Rs. 20.56 Arba.

The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 394.27 Arba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 19.71 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 40.44 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 39.84 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 33.35 Arba.

Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) ranked fourth with Rs. 31.95 Arba, while Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) stood fifth with Rs. 27.57 Arba. Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL) recorded the lowest reserve and surplus at Rs. 8.44 Arba, followed by Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) at Rs. 9.38 Arba and Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) at Rs. 9.63 Arba.

Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 7405.06 Arba in customer deposits, with seven banks surpassing the industry average of Rs. 370.25 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 686.14 Arba, followed by Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) at Rs. 669.17 Arba and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 592.56 Arba.

Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest customer deposits at Rs. 147.68 Arba, followed by Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) at Rs. 212.83 Arba and Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL) at Rs. 220.50 Arba.

Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 460.32 Arba, followed by Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) with Rs. 439.35 Arba and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) with Rs. 332.08 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) ranked fourth with Rs. 321.34 Arba.

Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest loan portfolio at Rs. 66.03 Arba, followed by Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) at Rs. 146.08 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement stood at Rs. 247.17 Arba, with seven banks exceeding this average.

Net interest income, a key indicator of core banking earnings, was highest at Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL), which recorded Rs. 17.00 Arba, followed by Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) at Rs. 16.20 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) ranked third with Rs. 12.98 Arba.

Banks recorded a total impairment charge of Rs. 37.30 Arba, reflecting provisions made for potential loan losses and credit-related risks. Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) posted the highest impairment charge at Rs. 6.19 Arba, followed by Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) at Rs. 4.94 Arba and Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) at Rs. 4.78 Arba.

Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 36.95, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 30.63 and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) at Rs. 29.14. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) ranked fourth with an EPS of Rs. 28.38, while Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded Rs. 28.17.

The industry average EPS stood at Rs. 18.64, with ten banks above this benchmark. Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) posted the lowest EPS at a negative Rs. 1.02, followed by NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) at Rs. 1.22 and Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) at Rs. 6.56.

Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the highest distributable profit per share at Rs. 38.32, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 20.85 and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 19.10. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) ranked fourth at Rs. 19.04.

Four banks reported negative distributable profit per share, with NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) recording the lowest at negative Rs. 99.65, followed by Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) at negative Rs. 43.58 and Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) at negative Rs. 26.82.

Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 358.68, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 287.70 and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 256.47. Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) ranked fourth with Rs. 247.28, while Agricultural Development Bank Limited (ADBL) stood fifth at Rs. 233.99.

Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 140.92, followed by Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) at Rs. 160.51. The industry average stood at Rs. 206.32.

Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) had the lowest P/E ratio at 7.46 times, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at 8.54 times and Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) at 12.22 times. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) recorded the highest P/E ratio at 266.90 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.

Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) at 18.13%, followed by Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) at 13.74% and Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at 13.66%. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) reported the lowest CAR at 11.10%, while the industry average stood at 12.85%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital position in relation to its risk-weighted assets.

Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.49%, while Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) reported the highest NPL at 15.55%. The industry average NPL stood at 5.44%.

Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest ROA at 16.49%, while Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) also reported the highest ROE at 1.51%. Everest Bank Limited (EBL) followed with an ROA of 14.41% and ROE of 1.32%.

- Costof Funds:Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) reported the highest cost of funds at 4.06%, while Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the lowest at 2.53%.

-CD Ratio:Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) recorded the highest CD ratio at 83.36%, followed by NMB Bank Limited (NMB) at 82.77%. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the lowest CD ratio at 47.24%.

-Base Rate:NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate at 5.83%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the lowest at 4.20%.

-Interest Spread:Everest Bank Limited (EBL) recorded the highest interest spread at 4.31%, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) at 3.77%. Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) had the lowest spread at 2.83%.

title: Gemini Recycle to Issue 10 Lakhs IPO Shares at NPR 190 (NPR 90 Premium)
content:
Gemini Recycle Nepal Limited has begun the process of issuing an initial public offering (IPO). During its special general meeting in Morang, the company approved a plan to offer 1 million shares representing 20 percent of its total issue capital of NPR 500 million to the general public. It also set the promoter share price at NPR 190 per share, which includes a face value of NPR 100 plus an NPR 90 premium.

Currently recycling old batteries, metals, and plastics for export primarily to India, the company plans to introduce technology to recycle electric vehicle (EV) batteries within Nepal to address upcoming battery waste. Led by business figure Diwakar Rathi alongside board members Aakash Golchha and Wil Kishor Menyangbo, Gemini Recycle is backed by major institutional investors. The company also aims to partner with public and private sectors to run waste collection via a mobile app.

title: Xiaomi Launches Redmi 17 Series in Nepal with 7,500mAh Battery and 120Hz Display
content:
Xiaomi has launched the Redmi 17 and Redmi 17 5G in Nepal, focusing on long battery life, smooth performance, and everyday durability. Both models feature a 7,500mAh battery, 45W turbo charging, 22.5W reverse charging, and a 6.9-inch 120Hz HD display.

The Redmi 17 is powered by the MediaTek Helio G91-Ultra, while the 5G variant uses the Snapdragon 4 Gen 5 platform. Both offer up to 12GB RAM with Memory Extension, a 50MP AI dual camera, 8MP selfie camera, stereo speakers, NFC, and IP64 protection.

The Redmi 17 starts at NPR 27,999, while the Redmi 17 5G starts at NPR 33,999, with higher storage variants priced up to NPR 41,999.

title: Indian Army Chief Meets Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Singha Durbar
content:
Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth paid a courtesy visit to Nepal's Prime Minister and Defense Minister Balendra Shah at the Prime Minister's Office in Singha Durbar, Kathmandu. The meeting included India's Ambassador to Nepal, Naveen Srivastava, and was confirmed by the Prime Minister's press expert, Deepa Dahal.

General Seth is on a four day official visit to Nepal with a five member delegation, including his spouse, Komal Seth, at the invitation of Nepal's Chief of Army Staff, General Ashok Raj Sigdel. During the visit, President Ramchandra Paudel conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army upon General Seth at Rastrapati Bhawan, continuing a reciprocal tradition between the two nations that dates back to 1950.

Additionally, General Seth held bilateral talks with General Sigdel to strengthen military relations, handed over medical and military equipment to the Nepali Army, and offered prayers at the Pashupatinath Temple. General Seth completes his visit and returns to India on Wednesday.
